voyage.name: Moore Park

This park is also the site of Sydney Boys High School and Sydney Girls High

voyage.name: Rushcutters Bay Park
voyage.phone: +61 2 9391-7000 (Monday to Friday 8AM-5PM), +61 293917000 (after hours service - Ranger or emergencies)
voyage.address: adjacent to Royal Cruising Yacht Club and extensive private mooring facilities at Rushcutters bay
voyage.content: Busy on weekends with walkers, people exersising their dogs by throwing balls and frisbees to them, picnickers sit about on the lawns and local people play come together to play informal ball games. The park caters for community sports such as cricket, rugby union and soccer. The park has a cafe and kiosk located toward the centre near the water that serves light meals, drinks and other refreshments.

voyage.name: McKell Park
voyage.price: Free entry with bookings and fees payable for Weddings and events
voyage.hours: Park gates are open from dawn to dusk (i.e. approximately 7AM - 7:30PM) Access is available to ferry services
voyage.address: at the northern end of Darling Point at the end of Darling Point Road
voyage.content: This small pretty park is the location of the Darling Point ferry wharf. The park comprises grassed landscape terraces stepping down to the harbour foreshore and the public ferry wharf. Set in the grounds of the original McKell mansion people picnic and relax amongst the footings and small remnant walls of the old mansion. It has become a popular site for weddings. The park was established in 1983-1985 with the herit

voyage.name: Nielsen Park
voyage.content: Established as a public reserve in 1911. Nearby is a 1.5-km 'Hermitage Foreshore' walk through park and bushland running along the western edge of Vaucluse between Nielsen Park and Bayview Hill Road. Has a scenic harbour swimming beach protected by a shark net during the summer months, picnic areas, meals and refreshments available at the Nielsen Park kiosk. See map and details of locality.

voyage.name: Bronte House
voyage.content: An historic house up Bronte Road from the north end of the beach.

voyage.name: Lindesay
voyage.price: $10 per adult, $5 per child (5–17)/concession holder, free for children under 5 and National Trust members.
voyage.hours: 45-minute tours run at 10AM and 11AM on the first and third Wednesdays of each month
voyage.content: One of Sydney's oldest residences with uninterrupted views of Sydney Harbour. The interior contains lots of colonial-style English furniture. It's a National Trust site today.

voyage.name: Vaucluse House
voyage.content: (Historic Houses Trust). Built in 1803, Vaucluse House is one of Sydney's oldest residences on a grand scale. The house and gardens are open to the public.

voyage.name: Play golf
voyage.content: In Moore Park.

voyage.name: Westfield Bondi Junction
voyage.content: One of the main shopping malls of Sydney, and easily the largest in the Eastern Suburbs, is right above the station in the heart of Bondi Junction. Hundreds of retailers and food outlets. Can be very busy. Take a walk outside the mall while you are there, the surrounding area, including Oxford Street Mall also contains a wide variety of shopping and eating destinations.

voyage.name: Doyles
voyage.content: Fish and chips at Watsons Bay, reservations are recommended. They also operate a takeaway just next to the wharf

voyage.name: Pizzavelly Italian Restaurant
voyage.content: Italian Pizzeria and Restaurant. View menu online.

voyage.name: Coogee Bay Hotel
voyage.address: Cnr of Coogee Bay Rd and Arden St
voyage.content: On a summer's day it is a great place to enjoy a relaxed drink or meal. There's an outdoor beer garden which is popular in summer, and kept warm in winter by outdoor heaters. In the evenings, it can get more lively, with live music, and a younger crowd of backpackers, locals and visitors from around Sydney.

voyage.name: Prince of Wales Hospital
voyage.content: The Public Hospital has 440 beds and almost 3,000 staff. The Prince of Wales Hospital has a relatively small but highly complex caseload with more than 30,000 acute patients admitted and about 40,000 patients treated in the Emergency Department annually.
